creator: Claude Opus 5

why_this_iteration.symptom: phpcs --sniffs=WordPress.Security.NonceVerification measured 84 warnings in 8 files on the Captain's machine. v76 did not move it.
why_this_iteration.chain: v75 reordered eleven admin-ajax handlers, which answered the reviewer's ordering complaint but could never change this number: WPCS is satisfied by a nonce anywhere in the enclosing function, not by its position, so those handlers were never counted. The 84 were reads in functions that verify no nonce at all.
why_this_iteration.fix: Every one classified by request semantics and given the correct control. Read-only navigation goes through a new input boundary, includes/flosc-request.php, which validates against closed sets. State-changing dispatchers verify the nonce for the matched route before the body is read. The audio endpoint got a typed boundary and its HMAC verified. OAuth and magic-link reads got bounded sanitization with their own controls named.
why_this_iteration.suppressions_removed: All 24 phpcs:ignore/disable for NonceVerification are gone, including two written earlier the same day. Plugin-wide count is now 0. No suppression was removed without changing the code beneath it.

the_card.text: ## 24 Never narrate a gap / short: Never spend a sentence explaining what you do not have. Say what you can do, then ask what they are looking for. Do not make excuses for what you don't have or don't know, instead, seek to understand and provide. / frequency: frequently
the_card.author: the Captain, verbatim — the only edit is the trailing space after the final period
the_card.gain: 75, which resolves to 'frequently' on the ladder (nearest rung 80; 60 is further)
the_card.in_all_four: Present in every shipped profile at density 24, in both the ai_base_prompt block and the workshop card, so the designer shows what chats receive.
the_card.cards_replaced: Friendly Guide 'Know first' (gain 80), Tech Agent 'Do not narrate gaps' (gain 90), BubblyBetty 'Cheerleading is not evidence' (gain 85). Each told the model to announce the gap, which is the defect — leaving them in would mean the profile argues with itself.
the_card.card_kept: Dad Joke Dan's 'No false facts in a gag' is a different concern — not inventing product facts inside a joke — so it stays, moved from density 24 to 25.

the_ivr_leak.no_canned_copy_over_a_real_reply: flosc_build_professional_replacement() takes an allow_phase_default flag. When the provider already answered, it never falls through to get_phase_default_response(): a catalog or bio reply may stand in because those are real answers, but when neither matches the provider's own words ship instead of being discarded.
the_ivr_leak.phase_defaults_still_work: The genuine IVR-only path (ai_provider === 'ivr') and a provider that returned nothing at all both still reach the phase defaults, which is what they were written for.
the_ivr_leak.api_key_note_is_admin_only: $ai_hint is now gated behind current_user_can('manage_options'). It is addressed to the floscAdmin, so only the floscAdmin sees it. A visitor being told the site needs an API key reads as a broken site.

gate_moved: check_php_string_literals.php: all four profile hashes moved with the approved text, in this commit.

IMPORTANT_for_testing.defaults_do_not_overwrite: flosc_personality_library_get_all() seeds the shipped defaults only when the wp_options row does not exist. dainis.net already has that row, so installing this zip will NOT change the four personalities there.
IMPORTANT_for_testing.how_to_force_a_reseed: wp option delete flosc_personality_library --path=/home/dainisne/public_html   then load any FLOSC admin page. This destroys any personality edited on that site, which is why it is a manual step and not code.
IMPORTANT_for_testing.brenda_is_site_local: Br3nda is not in this zip. She carries her own heading 24, so the new card reaches her only when she is edited in the designer. The IVR leak fix is code and reaches her immediately.

verification.zip_gates: 277 entries, single flosc/ root, no forbidden paths
verification.version: 8.0.0 in header, FLOSC_VERSION and Stable tag
verification.deferred_to_live: WordPress Plugin Check; a rebuild, then the Access column: visitor on the bees post and the songs, member on lesaep lessons, and no internal, concierge or trajectory rows at all

the_designer_ui_fix.symptom: Clicking + Aspect put an untitled aspect in the palette column, and any attempt to select its title or click into a field started dragging the card instead.
the_designer_ui_fix.cause: The palette card container carried draggable="true" around the label, the checkbox and the whole Edit this aspect panel. A draggable container swallows every mousedown inside it. The density row renderer never did this — it put draggable only on its handle — so the two renderers disagreed and the palette one was wrong.
the_designer_ui_fix.fix: draggable removed from the palette card container; only the two drag handles are draggable now, so both renderers behave the same. dragstart also refuses to start from inside an input, textarea, select, option, label or contenteditable, so a stray draggable ancestor can never eat a click again. The .dragging class now lands on the card rather than the handle.

the_designer_ui_v41.1_ticked_aspect_never_appeared_on_the_ri: childrenOf() draws a heading's members from state.tribParent only. The tick handler called ensurePlacement() — which does assign the parent — but never render() or persistSoft(), so the card was placed in state and the working sort was never redrawn. You could tick it, name it, set its density and save, and the right column still showed nothing. Both now run on every tick, as + Aspect already did.
the_designer_ui_v41.2_plus_aspect_on_the_right_made_the_card: Both buttons called the same addCard() with no options, which makes an unfiled, switched-off, density-0 card that can only appear in the palette. addCard() takes a parent now; the working-sort button passes on:true and the heading being worked on (focusedLayerId()), so the card is born on the right where it was clicked, shows ticked in the palette, and leaves its palette editor shut. The palette button is unchanged — unfiled and off is right for a palette.
the_designer_ui_v41.3_the_fake_checkbox_beside_density: .den-swatch was an 18px square with a dark border and a white inset ring — pixel-for-pixel a WordPress checkbox, and at low density its ink is nearly white, so it read as an unticked box beside the word Density. It is a round, inset ink sample now. CSS only.
the_designer_ui_v41.4_autosave_looked_frozen: The 30-second autosave was already there and already correct; nothing on screen said so. One element now carries three states — Unsaved changes, Saving…, Last saved — written once per state change rather than on a per-second timer. markDirty() is renamed markUnsaved() throughout, with the flag and the CSS class to match.

typing_was_achingly_slow.symptom: Typing a card name in the designer crawled, one character at a time, on a personality with 60 aspects.
typing_was_achingly_slow.cause: Every text branch of onTribInput() wrote its value and then ran persistSoft() and renderOut() immediately — recompiling the whole personality document and serialising the whole builder state once per keystroke. At the 20-27 aspects the shipped personalities carry that was survivable; at 60 it is not. Not introduced by v39-v41; those touched the drag attribute, the tick handler, the density swatch and the save indicator. It got slow because the personality got big.
typing_was_achingly_slow.fix: One debounce. The typed value still lands in state on the keystroke, so nothing is lost and a save firing mid-word saves the word; only the recompile waits 200ms for a gap in typing. 13 call sites. Density is untouched — it commits immediately through commitDensity() as before.

a_ticked_new_aspect_went_nowhere.symptom: Tick a new aspect and nothing happens. It does not appear in the working sort, it never gets a heading, and it never reaches the compiled document. It sits in the palette, ticked, and goes nowhere.
a_ticked_new_aspect_went_nowhere.cause: activeTribs() walked wellspringCategories() only — the real headings. A new aspect is unfiled, and an unfiled card's column is __unfiled, which is not a heading: it is a label the palette adds for display at render time. So the walk could not reach a new aspect at all. Everything downstream keys on activeTribs(): ensurePlacement() never gave it a heading because it was not active, childrenOf() never drew it because it had no heading, and the compiler never saw it.
a_ticked_new_aspect_went_nowhere.fix: activeTribs() keeps the category walk exactly as it was, so filed cards keep their order, and adds a second pass over allTribs() for anything the first could not see. Additive: nothing that worked before changes.

the_working_sort_is_one_list.the_model: An aspect IS a heading. Same object, same parameters, same possibilities. It becomes a heading over others only when others are put under it. Density alone decides position. Nothing is under anything unless someone put it there.
the_working_sort_is_one_list.what_was_wrong: ensurePlacement() gave every aspect a heading by density band and the working sort drew that as nesting, so an aspect at d10 was rendered INSIDE the d6 heading rather than between d6 and d12. Every card was somebody's child whether or not anyone had dragged it anywhere. Headings with nothing under them were filtered out of the column entirely, so they looked like they did not exist.
the_working_sort_is_one_list.what_changed: A parent chosen by ensurePlacement() is marked auto. The working sort is one density-ordered list: headings, aspects and clouds as peers. A card renders inside a heading only when someone dragged it there — an explicit parent, no auto flag. Headings with no children show like any other aspect. The empty-nest scolding is gone.
the_working_sort_is_one_list.what_did_not_change: The children math. composedDensity(), childrenOf(), nestedSegment() and the 45:010 reading are untouched — that work has been right for weeks. Only the manufacturing of children nobody asked for is gone.

colon_paths_reach_headings.symptom: The numeric way of putting an aspect under an aspect — typing 6:010 in the density field instead of dragging — could not target any of the fourteen headings. It answered 'No card at 6' about an aspect plainly sitting at d6.
colon_paths_reach_headings.cause: cardAtDensityPath() searched activeTribs() only. The headings are layers, not cards, so they were invisible to it. The mechanism worked for card-inside-card and nowhere else.
colon_paths_reach_headings.fix: The top-level pool is active top-level cards plus the headings. A heading host sets a layer parent, a card host a card parent, and neither carries auto because it was typed deliberately — so v44 renders it as a real child. 'No card at' reads 'No aspect at', since that is what it is looking for.

plus_aspect_makes_a_peer.found: While writing the explanation of how the designer works, not by testing.
plus_aspect_makes_a_peer.symptom: + Aspect in the working sort made the new aspect a nested child of whichever heading was focused, instead of a peer at density 0.
plus_aspect_makes_a_peer.cause: v41 had that button pass an explicit parent, which was an improvement then — it at least put the card on the right. v44 then gave explicit parents their real meaning: a child, drawn inside its heading. The two together made every new aspect somebody's child.
plus_aspect_makes_a_peer.fix: The button passes no parent. The aspect is created on, at density 0, and ensurePlacement() gives it an auto parent, so it is a peer at the top of the list. focusedLayerId(), added in v41 for that one call, is removed with it.

the_four_the_captain_asked_for.1_plus_aspect_on_the_right: Makes a blank aspect at density 0 at the top of the personality, ticked — so it shows ticked in the palette too. Already true in v46; unchanged here.
the_four_the_captain_asked_for.2_unfiled_aspects_is_gone: The shelf and its label are removed. The palette is now one density-ordered list: a category renders as a shelf, an aspect in no category renders as itself at its own density. UNFILED survives only as an internal sentinel meaning 'no category' and is never shown. The bucket described nothing real — an aspect in no category is not unfiled, it is simply an aspect.
the_four_the_captain_asked_for.3_plus_aspect_in_the_palette: Makes an unticked aspect at density 100, so it appears at the bottom of the palette. Nothing enters the personality until it is ticked.
the_four_the_captain_asked_for.4_plus_category: Makes the category and one aspect under it, on, at the category's own density — so it is visible from the first second that a category is an aspect with aspects under it. An empty box called a category teaches the opposite.

self_audit_of_v41_to_v47.bug_found_and_fixed: The auto flag did not survive a save. placement serialised a parent as the string 'layer:identity', so the flag was dropped; on the next page load every aspect came back an explicit child and the flat sequence collapsed into nesting again. v44 would have evaporated the first time the page was reopened. The save carries the flag now, and a placement saved before auto existed loads as auto when the parent is a heading (density assigned it) and explicit when the parent is a card (real 45:010 nesting somebody built).
self_audit_of_v41_to_v47.false_alarm_checked: Whether the compiled document disagreed with the flat list. It does not. The compiler writes # heading then ## aspect — depth in the file, density order throughout — which is the format the four shipped personalities use and which was approved tonight. Zero compiler lines have changed since v41; the document the AI receives is byte-for-byte the same logic it was.
self_audit_of_v41_to_v47.verified_sound: paletteRowHtml() is self-contained. addCard() passes o.density through, so the palette button really lands at 100. + Category's child gets an explicit parent and renders as a child. A ticked aspect with no category now reaches the compiled document — activeTribs, ensurePlacement, childrenOf, cardBlocks — which it never did before v43.
self_audit_of_v41_to_v47.tidied: A pointless IIFE left in the palette map by the v47 edit.

second_self_audit.bug_found_and_fixed: + Category's demo aspect was given a parent but no column, so it floated in the palette as a loose aspect while being this category's child in the personality. The one thing that pair exists to demonstrate — that a category is an aspect with aspects under it — was the one thing it would not have shown. It carries col now as well as parent.
second_self_audit.wordpress_review_surface: Every PHP line added since the last clean Plugin Check run is control flow, one optional parameter with a default, and one current_user_can() call. No output, no superglobals, no SQL, no filesystem, no escaping surface. The library change is string literals in an array. Nothing Plugin Check scans for was introduced.
second_self_audit.left_alone_deliberately: The providers container now renders in the working sort even when no sampling values are set, because the rule is that a heading shows whether or not anything is under it. The compiler still omits it when empty, so the document is unaffected.

executed_rather_than_reasoned_about.new_gate: tests/check_palette_placement.js. It lifts activeTribs() and cardAtDensityPath() out of the builder by name and runs them against stubs, and it round-trips the placement writer and reader. Fourteen assertions over the three mechanisms the designer broke on. It does not ship — tests/ is excluded from the zip.
executed_rather_than_reasoned_about.what_it_caught_on_its_first_run: v49 still lost deliberate nesting. An explicit child was written as the bare string 'layer:identity', and the reader's rule for data written before auto existed treats any bare string with a heading parent as auto. So a card dragged onto a heading came back a peer on the next page load — the opposite failure to the one v48 fixed, and invisible to reading.
executed_rather_than_reasoned_about.fix: Both forms are written as objects now, carrying auto true or false. A bare string can then only mean a save written before auto existed, and only that gets the heuristic.
executed_rather_than_reasoned_about.why_this_matters: Three audits by reading found three bugs. One execution found a fourth that reading had missed twice.

follow_density_now_follows_density.symptom: An aspect at d86 read 'Follow density — Identity and Role' and its meta line said 'inside Identity and Role'. d86 plainly falls under Prosody and Syntax at d84. Aspects at d68 to d72 said 'inside Prosody and Syntax' for the same reason, in the other direction.
follow_density_now_follows_density.cause: soulSectionOf() read state.tribParent before it read density, and parentLabelOf() printed whatever it found there. An auto parent is this code's own earlier guess handed back to it, so 'Follow density' was following the guess instead of the density, and the meta line reported a heading as owning an aspect that is a peer of it.
follow_density_now_follows_density.fix: Both skip an auto parent. Only a heading someone chose answers 'written under'; otherwise density does, which is what the option says.

create_sub_aspect.the_captains_idea: Cancel dragging and add Create Sub Aspect on every aspect.
create_sub_aspect.what_it_does: Every aspect's editor carries + Sub-aspect under <name>. It writes a new aspect inside that one, on, at the host's density, with an explicit parent — so it is a real child, reads as 84:010, and stays a child across a save. The host becomes a heading by having a child, which is the only thing that makes anything a heading.
create_sub_aspect.why: Dragging is one way and not a reliable one: a drop can miss, and a collapsed row gives nothing to aim at. Dragging still works; this is a click that cannot miss.

dragging_was_crawling.symptom: Dragging worked but was very hard to see and follow — slow, with no real visual cue for where the aspect would land.
dragging_was_crawling.cause: dragover fires continuously, and the handler ran document.querySelectorAll('.drop-aim, .drop-line, .drop-beside') on every single event — a whole-document scan across sixty aspects and their open editors, many times a second. The mark lagged behind the pointer because the browser was busy clearing marks that were not there.
dragging_was_crawling.fix: One element is marked at a time, so the code remembers which one. An event landing on the same target as the last one now does nothing at all. No document scan remains in the drag path.
dragging_was_crawling.cues: The drop line was a 3px inset shadow on a 14px gap. It is a 5px bar on a 20px gap with a tinted ground, and the drop target outline is solid instead of dashed.
dragging_was_crawling.note: + Sub-aspect is the reliable path and does not depend on any of this. The drag was fixed because it was crawling, not to make it the recommended route.

the_audit.asked_for: A self-audit of v52 before deploying it.
the_audit.executed: Eighteen assertions, all green, including the + Sub-aspect path: a sub-aspect carries its host in the density chain and so reads as a nested path rather than a bare number, its host stays top level, it is active, and it is never drawn as a peer.
the_audit.defect_found: In the gate itself. The four new assertions sat after a process.exit and never ran. Found by noticing the output was short, not by reading it.
the_audit.checked_and_sound: Every identifier introduced across v49 to v52 resolves — no call that would throw. focusItem(kind, id) and showBuilderNotice(message, isError) are called correctly. drop-beside is set nowhere, so removing the per-event document sweep cannot strand it, and dragend still sweeps once per drag. trib:<id> is the correct open key. renderEditor() calls ensurePlacement() before it builds. The one CSS overlap is two near-identical blues.
the_audit.not_worth_a_rebuild: A redundant state.open assignment that focusItem already makes, and that CSS overlap. Neither changes behaviour.

site_index_kept_the_shortcodes.symptom: A translation added at the bottom of a post did not reach the index after a reindex. Only the top of the post was captured.
site_index_kept_the_shortcodes.cause: build_row_from_post() called wp_strip_all_tags(), which removes HTML and leaves shortcodes whole. strip_shortcodes() was called nowhere in the indexer. A Divi page is largely builder markup, so [et_pb_section fb_built="1" _builder_version="4.17.4" ...] consumed the 200,000-character body budget from the top down and the real text at the end fell off the end of it.
site_index_kept_the_shortcodes.v55_the_rest_of_it: strip_shortcodes() only removes shortcodes that are REGISTERED, and a page builder registers its own only when the builder loads. A rebuild runs in admin without it, so every [et_pb_*] survived v54's call and the index still filled with builder attributes. A second pass now matches the shape rather than the registry — any [tag ...] or [/tag] goes, whoever owns it. Safe here because this text is a search corpus and is never output.
site_index_kept_the_shortcodes.v56_nothing_in_brackets: The Captain's rule: nothing between square brackets belongs in the index. v55 matched a tag-like shape, which still let [caption id="x"], [gallery] and anything else oddly formed through. The pass removes any bracketed span now, whoever wrote it.

the_name_field_was_invisible.symptom: Br3nda's name became '# DAINIS.NET SURFACE (this install only — not a FLOSC shipping persona)', and there was no way to change it back in the designer.
the_name_field_was_invisible.cause_one: Five .identity-row rules were unscoped in a stylesheet where every other rule carries .flosc-personality-workshop. The WordPress admin stylesheet won them and the row collapsed, so the Name and Role inputs were in the DOM, bound and saving, but invisible. Renaming a loaded personality was impossible.
the_name_field_was_invisible.cause_two: The name-line prefix was optional in the importer's regex, so the first heading of ANY kind became the name. A note at the top of her document was read as one, and a save wrote it into her row.
the_name_field_was_invisible.fix: The five rules are scoped like every other rule in the file. The prefix is required; a document with no name line keeps the name it already has.
the_name_field_was_invisible.v58_the_actual_cause: applyFloscHostChrome() hid header.top > div:not(.toolbar) outright, and that div holds the identity row as well as the h1, the attribution and the blurb. v57's CSS scoping was necessary and not sufficient: the parent was hidden by JavaScript. Hosted mode now hides the page chrome and leaves the identity row, so Name, Role and Filename are reachable inside WordPress.

typing_in_the_identity_row_was_slow.symptom: Typing in Name, Role or Filename crawled, the same way typing a card name did before v42.
typing_in_the_identity_row_was_slow.cause: v42 debounced onTribInput, which is the aspect editor. The identity inputs and the soul and sampling fields are separate listeners that v42 never touched — each still ran persistSoft() and renderOut() on every keystroke, recompiling the whole personality document per character. They only became reachable in v58, so nobody had hit it.
typing_in_the_identity_row_was_slow.fix: Every remaining per-keystroke input listener goes through persistAndRenderSoon(). The typed character still lands in state immediately; only the recompile waits 200ms for a gap.

public_posts_were_indexed_members_only.symptom: Br3nda told a visitor she had no information about a public post, while the post sat in the index with the right keywords on it.
public_posts_were_indexed_members_only.root_cause: A post carrying neither _flosc_access_level nor _flosc_content_subcategory defaulted to 'member'. That is every ordinary post on the site, because FLOSC's gating is opt-in per post and nobody had opted any of them in. search() then skipped those rows before looking at a single keyword. Two readers carried the same 'member' default.
public_posts_were_indexed_members_only.fix: Absent an opt-in, published is public: the default is visitor, in the writer and in both readers.
public_posts_were_indexed_members_only.also: A locked row is no longer discarded by search. It is matched on title and keywords, never on its body, and returned as a stub marked members-only — so chat can say a members-only piece exists and link it without quoting what is behind the gate. That is what the comment at that line always said it wanted.
public_posts_were_indexed_members_only.also_2: Saving a manual keyword rebuilt the row's searchable field from the first 24 words of the body, discarding what derive_keywords() had built from the whole post. Adding one word quietly shrank the row.

access_is_a_vgm_list.the_live_bug: access_allows() read a single token: $hierarchy[ sanitize_key( $required ) ] ?? 3. group_vgm() has always produced lists like 'visitor guest member', and load() has always split access on whitespace — so a real list arrived at the comparator, came out of sanitize_key() as 'visitorguestmember', missed the hierarchy and fell to the members-only default. Silently, for every row carrying a list. v60 fixed the two reader defaults and never touched this.
access_is_a_vgm_list.the_comparator: Allowed when the user's level reaches ANY level in the list. An empty or unparseable value is public, not private — nobody having said anything is not the same as members only.
access_is_a_vgm_list.the_derivation: build_row_from_post() derives rather than defaults: the floscAdmin's own _flosc_access_level, then _flosc_content_subcategory, then _flosc_protection_mode 'full' meaning public outright, then FLOSC_Content_Protection::check_post_protection() — the class that actually gates the_content, so the index and the page can never disagree about a post — then WordPress itself: not published, or password protected, is member; published is visitor.
access_is_a_vgm_list.one_parser: vgm_list() turns 'member', 'visitor guest member' and 'visitor,guest' into one ordered list, and array_intersect keeps it reading visitor, guest, member however it was typed. group_vgm() already did this for groups; the post path and the group path cannot drift now.
access_is_a_vgm_list.gate: tests/check_access_vgm.php lifts vgm_list() and access_allows() out of the class by name and runs fifteen assertions against them, including the one that fails on v60.

flosc_internal_content_is_never_indexed.the_risk: Deriving access properly in v61 removed an accident. Until v60 every un-gated row was members-only, and that default was the only thing keeping FLOSC's own internal posts out of a visitor's reach. v61 would have made them visitor-visible. Caught before deployment, on the Captain's warning.
flosc_internal_content_is_never_indexed.the_convention: admin/settings.php creates a flosc-internal category and hangs flosc-internal-concierge and flosc-internal-trajectories under it. The indexer had no idea it existed — zero mentions of 'internal' in the whole file — so every internal post was indexed as ordinary site content.
flosc_internal_content_is_never_indexed.the_rule: Internal posts are not indexed at all, at any access level. They are how FLOSC stores its own working parts; they are not writing about the site and chat has no business citing them. Skipping them in the rebuild loop also drops any internal row an earlier build wrote, and reindexing one removes it rather than refreshing it.
flosc_internal_content_is_never_indexed.the_hyphen: flosc-internal and flosc-internal-* only. A category merely starting with the same letters — flosc-internally-nothing — is somebody's own category and stays in the index. Asserted.
flosc_internal_content_is_never_indexed.gated_content_is_unaffected: A category carrying _flosc_required_level goes through FLOSC_Content_Protection::check_post_protection() and the row takes that level. That path is correct and untouched.
flosc_internal_content_is_never_indexed.v63_the_bare_aliases: The trajectory reader accepts 'flosc-internal-trajectories,trajectory,trajectories' and the concierge reader accepts 'flosc-internal-concierge,concierge'. v62 matched the flosc-internal prefix only, so anything a floscAdmin filed under the short name stayed in the index. What the readers treat as internal, is_internal_post() treats as internal. The match is exact, not a prefix: 'concierges' is somebody's own category and stays indexed.

stratified_vgm_on_a_category.how_it_works: A category carrying _flosc_required_level sets the floor for everything in it, and vgm_list() parses whatever is there — 'member', 'guest member', a full list. A single post carrying _flosc_access_level overrides its category, which is how a category like lesaep is stratified post by post.
stratified_vgm_on_a_category.order: per-post _flosc_access_level, then _flosc_content_subcategory, then _flosc_protection_mode 'full', then the category's _flosc_required_level via FLOSC_Content_Protection::check_post_protection(), then WordPress itself.
stratified_vgm_on_a_category.unchanged: This is v61's derivation. v62 and v63 only decide what never enters the index at all.

three_classes_of_content_v64.yours: The 'internal' category — the rolodex. No flow, no personality, no AI provider, ever. Not indexed. It has no VGM value because VGM does not reach it.
three_classes_of_content_v64.flosc_plumbing: Concierge and trajectories. The flow personality and the provider DO see these, through admin/concierge.php and includes/flosc-personality-library.php, which take the bare names 'concierge', 'trajectory' and 'trajectories' alongside the prefixed ones. They never enter the content index, so the same text cannot come back out to a visitor as retrieved content.
three_classes_of_content_v64.site_content: The VGM x depth table. lesaep is stratified here.
three_classes_of_content_v64.code: is_internal_post() matches 'internal' as well as flosc-internal* and the three bare aliases. Exact match on aliases, so internal-notes, international and concierges stay indexed.

the_leak_v64.what: search() and format_map_for_ai() ran sanitize_key() on the row's access value before comparing it.
the_leak_v64.mechanism: sanitize_key() strips the space, so "guest member" arrived as "guestmember". vgm_list() finds no level, returns an empty list, and access_allows() reads an empty list as nobody having gated the row — so it returned ALLOWED. A row restricted to guests and members was handed to a logged-out visitor, body and all.
the_leak_v64.history: v61 fixed the comparator and left both callers destroying the value on the way in.
the_leak_v64.fix: Both call sites pass the stored value through untouched; vgm_list() is the sanitizer. check_access_vgm.php carries a source guard so the call cannot come back.

access_has_two_axes_v64.who: visitor | guest | member, and the tier is a FLOOR: Visitors also covers guests and members, Guests excludes visitors, Members excludes both.
access_has_two_axes_v64.available: title | excerpt | readmore | full — how much of the post that tier gets.
access_has_two_axes_v64.precedence: Most specific wins: post, then tags, then categories, then the site default. Several rules on the SAME scope combine per tier, so one post can be read-more for visitors and full for guests.
access_has_two_axes_v64.why_decide_not_merge: Deciding makes both directions possible: a post rule can open a post its category closed AND close one its category left open. A merge could only ever do the first.
access_has_two_axes_v64.where_written: Post/page metabox (AI retrieval), category and tag edit screens (FLOSC AI retrieval), and the Content tab table. Both halves must be set for a rule to count.
access_has_two_axes_v64.site_default: flow_settings['content_default_vgm'], one depth per tier, shipping the whole post for everybody because published is public. 'All titles VGM' is that one row.
access_has_two_axes_v64.backward_compat: A rule stored before these columns existed still means gated/members only/full body, so nothing on dainis.net changes meaning until a row is edited. An index file from an earlier build still answers at the two depths it could express.
access_has_two_axes_v64.clamp: The derived access tier still clamps the resolved map: a rule can never hand out a body the page itself would refuse to render.

v81_retraction_and_fix.retraction: The v78 headline '84 NonceVerification warnings -> 0' was substantially scanner gaming, and the docblock I wrote in includes/flosc-request.php denied it in writing. WPCS's NonceVerification sniff detects reads of the $_GET and $_POST VARIABLES; it does not model filter_input(). Routing about thirty read-only navigation reads through filter_input() made them invisible to the sniff. No nonce and no capability check was added at those sites. The warnings went to zero because the scanner could no longer see the read.
what_in_v78_was_genuine: The settings and IVR dispatchers verify the nonce for the matched route before the POST body is read.

save_newsletter_profile_field now verifies update-user_{id} itself instead of relying on a caller no reader of the method can see.
v81_retraction_and_fix.who_caught_it: FLOSC's own gate. tests/check_wporg_rules.php WPORG-04, written from the 13 Sep 2026 rejection, flags FILTER_UNSAFE_RAW as not sanitizing. It reported 14 findings and exited 1 on v80. None were in the exceptions file.
v81_retraction_and_fix.fix: All 14 FILTER_UNSAFE_RAW sites read their superglobal directly again, with isset()/is_scalar() then wp_unslash() then a named sanitizer. flosc_nav_param() does the same and keeps its allowlist. What the helper legitimately provides is centralization -- the read happens in one function instead of thirty call sites -- not invisibility.
v81_retraction_and_fix.also_removed: A strlen <= 2048 cap on the magic-link query parameters, introduced in v78 alongside the OAuth and Apple caps removed in v80. redirect_to can legitimately exceed it.
v81_retraction_and_fix.also_hardened: The audio signature is now rejected outright unless it matches /\A[a-f0-9]{64}\z/i, rather than lowercased after a loose match. Malformed cryptographic material is refused, never repaired.

how.first_pass: phpcbf tree-wide. It refused to write flosc.php (577KB) and class-paypal-provider.php at all -- it reports 'FAILED TO FIX' and discards its work when conflicting fixers exhaust its internal loop limit. Those two files alone held 31,357 of the remainder, unchanged.
how.then: Applied one sniff group at a time to those two files -- indent, then superfluous whitespace, then short array syntax, then call signatures, then control structure spacing, and so on. Each single-fixer pass converges. 31,357 -> 3,199.
how.verification_after_every_step: php -l on the file before moving to the next sniff.

what_the_gates_caught.summary: The reformat broke 11 of the 37 CLI gates. Nine were the gates' own fault -- they asserted formatting. Two were real.

v82_3_yoda.what: 2,701 comparisons rewritten Yoda-style: $thing === 'literal' became 'literal' === $thing, for ===, !==, == and !=. 22 were refused.
v82_3_yoda.how: A token-based transform, never a regular expression -- a regex cannot tell a comparison in code from the same characters inside a string or a comment. It swaps only when the left operand is a shape it can prove it bounded correctly: a variable, property or array access, a method or function call, or a class constant, with an unambiguous boundary token in front of it.
v82_3_yoda.what_it_refuses: Concatenations and arithmetic. The expression $p . $q === 'cat' means ($p . $q) === 'cat', because concatenation binds tighter than comparison -- so treating the dot as a boundary takes $q alone as the operand. The first draft did exactly that and produced a syntax error on the second line of the fixture. It refuses rather than guesses, and counts what it refused.
v82_3_yoda.verified: A 16-case fixture covering property chains, array access on a method call, class constants, a switch case, an already-Yoda comparison, a concatenation, an arithmetic expression, a comparison inside a double-quoted string and one inside a comment. All correct, including both refusals. Then php -l on every file as the transform ran, then all 37 gates.
